subject: Recap & next steps — NovaPay discovery (pricing & token volumes)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — NovaPay discovery (pricing & token volumes)

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

- Current ask: evaluate Redwood for customer-facing chat and a few high-volume enrichment jobs.
- Key constraints: predictable unit economics, ability to hit a target $/1M tokens, and clear invoicing for procurement.
- Preliminary volume estimate from call: baseline 5–10M tokens/month, expected growth to 15–20M in 6–12 months (you mentioned a high-traffic event).

Open items for us to size an invoice estimate:
1) Confirm the expected monthly token band you want us to price to (you gave low/typical/peak ranges on the call).
2) Target $/1M tokens you need to hit to make this budget work.
3) Procurement timeline and contact for contract/invoice routing.

If you can reply with those three items I’ll have a draft cost model and invoice estimate back to you by EOD tomorrow. I’ll include a couple of scenarios (pay-as-you-go vs. committed reserved capacity) and an attachment with a simple calculator.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
redwood.inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novapay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@novapay.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — NovaPay discovery (pricing & token volumes)

Sean — thanks for the recap. Confirming the items from our side:

- Monthly token band: typical 8–12M tokens/month, with short peaks up to ~20M for big customer campaigns.
- Target unit economics: we’re aiming for roughly $150–$200 / 1M tokens (this gets us to budget targets for the Q4 roadmap).
- Procurement: moving fast; procurement@novapay.com handles initial review. I’ll loop Sophie (sophie.lee@novapay.com) for contract follow-up.

Also: can you include a monthly invoice estimate for 8M, 12M, and 20M tokens and a note on committed capacity discounts (12-month vs 36-month)? We’ll also want to understand outage SLA and whether committed capacity can be region-locked to us-east-1.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’d like something formal we can share with procurement.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of Product | NovaPay
alex.johnson@novapay.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novapay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@novapay.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — NovaPay discovery (pricing & token volumes)

Alex / team — attaching the cost model and a one-page invoice estimate as requested. Attachments: novapay_cost_model_v3.xlsx (cost calculator) and invoice_estimate_202706.pdf (one-page).

High-level unit economics (example profile used in the attached model):
- Raw inference compute (model kernels + GPU cycles): $80 / 1M tokens
- Serving infra, KV cache and orchestration overhead: $40 / 1M tokens
- Support, monitoring, observability and retention: $10 / 1M tokens
- Commercial margin / account services: $20 / 1M tokens
=> Total illustrative price: $150 / 1M tokens

Sample monthly invoice estimates (illustrative, USD):
- 8M tokens/month x $150 / 1M = $1,200 / month
- 12M tokens/month x $150 / 1M = $1,800 / month
- 20M tokens/month x $150 / 1M = $3,000 / month

Committed capacity (examples):
- 12-month commit: ~10% discount vs list above (subject to contract)
- 36-month commit: ~18% discount vs list above

Notes & assumptions (see attached model for line-by-line):
- Token definition: 1 token ≈ 4 chars; all pricing shown is per processed input+output tokens.
- Model mix: estimates assume a mid-capacity model variant the team discussed; switching to a higher-cost model increases the raw inference line.
- Billing: monthly invoicing in USD; enterprise billing terms (net-30) are supported.
- Region: we can region-lock dedicated pools to us-east-1 for compliance/regional latency guarantees.

Next suggested steps:
1) Please confirm which token band you want formalized in the SOW (8 / 12 / 20M).
2) Confirm procurement contact and preferred contract term (12 vs 36 months).
3) I’ll create a DocuSign-ready SOW and a committed-capacity appendix once we have the band & term.

Links:
- Cost model (live): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcD-example-cost-model
- Draft SOW / DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/agreements/ZXCV-12345

Attachments (stubs):
- novapay_cost_model_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 124 KB)
- invoice_estimate_202706.pdf (application/pdf, 46 KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Lead Pricing Analyst | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0177

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novapay.com>

Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — NovaPay discovery (pricing & token volumes)

Marissa / Sean — this looks good, thanks. I’ve looped Sophie from procurement (sophie.lee@novapay.com) into the thread. Procurement will review the invoice estimate and the attached cost model. A few quick notes:

- Procurement prefers monthly invoicing in USD and would like the option to convert to a committed reserved capacity addendum within 30 days of signing.
- Can you include a 30-day eval credit in the SOW (we typically request a short pilot window to validate latency and correctness)?
- Also confirm whether Redwood can issue invoices with EU VAT formatting if we later spin up a dedicated pool in eu-west-1.

Procurement will get back to us early next week — please prepare a DocuSign SOW with the 12-month committed term (we’ll markup if needed).

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product | NovaPay
